[[File:Lyn Evans - pictures donated by CERN-11.jpg|thumb|Lyn Evans in his role as the LHC Project leader (2008)]]
'''Lyndon Rees Evans''' (born 1945) is a Welsh scientist who served as the project leader of the [[Large Hadron Collider]] in Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Krause |first=Michael |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/9789814623476_0006 |title=CERN: How We Found the Higgs Boson |date=2014 |publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC |isbn=978-981-4623-55-1 |language=en |chapter=The Man Who Built the LHC: Lyn Evans |pages=98–107 |doi=10.1142/9789814623476_0006}}</ref> Based at [[CERN]], in 2012 he became the director of the Linear Collider Collaboration, an international organisation managing development of next generation particle colliders, including the [[International Linear Collider]] and the [[Compact Linear Collider]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|date=July 2012|title=Lyn Evans becomes Linear Collider director|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734828|journal=CERN Courier|volume=52|issue=6|page=37}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born and raised in [[Cwmbach]] near [[Aberdare]] in the [[South Wales Valleys]], Evans had an interest in [[chemistry]] in his youth, initially enrolling in university to study the subject before switching to [[physics]] because he found the subject easier.<ref name="Scientist in charge of collider">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/7806444.stm|title=Scientist in charge of collider|work=BBC Wales|access-date=26 July 2009 | date=2 January 2009}}</ref> Evans was educated at [[Aberdare Boys' Grammar School]], where he developed an interest in physics. However, he found it difficult to pass his [[O Level]] in French, a qualification which was required to allow him to enter his course at the University College of Swansea (now [[Swansea University]]), from where he graduated in 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/wales/scifiles/interviewsub/liveevans.shtml|title=Lyn Evans|work=BBC Scifiles|access-date=5 December 2008}}</ref> He switched to physics in his second year of undergraduate study at Swansea.<ref name="Scientist in charge of collider"/> He went to CERN initially as a research fellow, having previously visited the establishment in 1969 as a visitor.<ref name="Scientist in charge of collider"/>

In 1994,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/uk/science/article4719786.ece|title=Welsh engineer leads the way in Large Hadron Collider project|work=The Times|date=10 September 2008|access-date=5 December 2008 | location=London | first=Mark | last=Henderson}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> he became involved in the planning of the project which would become the Large Hadron Collider. He served as the LHC project leader until 2008.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.southwales-eveningpost.co.uk/aberdare-born-physicist-who-built-the-large-hadron-collider-to-speak-at-swansea-festival/story-29457938-detail/story.html|title=Physicist who built Large Hadron Collider talks at city festival|date=29 June 2016|newspaper=South Wales Evening Post|access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref> In 2011 at the international symposium on subnuclear physics held in Vatican City, he gave a talk ''The Proton Beam for the Neutrino Velocity Measurement with OPERA''.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Sánchez Sorondo, Marcelo|editor-link=Marcelo Sánchez Sorondo|editor2=Zichichi, Antonino|editor-link2=Antonino Zichichi|chapter=''The Proton Beam for the Neutrino Velocity Measurement with OPERA'' by Lyndon Evans|pages=337–342|title=Subnuclear Physics: Past, Present and Future; Proceedings of the International Symposium, held 30 October - 2 November 2011, held in Vatican City|series=Scripta Varia, volume 119|publisher=[[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]|year=2014|chapter-url=https://www.pas.va/content/dam/casinapioiv/pas/pdf-volumi/scripta-varia/sv119/sv119-evans.pdf}}</ref>

In June 2012, the International Committee for Future Accelerators selected Evans as Director of the Linear Collider Collaboration, an international effort promoting construction of a new linear collider to complement CERN's Large Hadron Collider.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honours==
*Evans has been a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] since 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1991&unit_id=DPB&institution=CERN|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=aps.org|access-date=19 December 2016}}</ref>
*He was appointed CBE in the [[2001 New Year Honours]].
*He was made an honorary fellow of the University of Wales Swansea in 2002.<ref>{{cite journal|date=November 2002|title=People|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733402|journal=CERN Courier|volume=42|issue=9|page=45}}</ref> 
*He was awarded an honorary Doctor of Science from the [[University of Glamorgan]] (now [[University of South Wales]]) in July 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.glam.ac.uk/news/en/2009/jul/14/honorary-doctorate-welsh-physicist/|title=Honorary Doctorate for Welsh Physicist, News Centre|website=news.glam.ac.uk|access-date=19 December 2016}}</ref>
*In 2010, Evans was also elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/lyndon-evans-11413/|title=Lyndon Evans|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=19 December 2016}}</ref>
*In 2011, Evans was elected a [[Learned Society of Wales|Fellow of the Learned Society of Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=The Learned Society of |title=Lyn Evans |url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/lyn-evans/ |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=The Learned Society of Wales |language=en-US}}</ref>
*On 11 December 2012, he was awarded the 2012 Special [[Fundamental Physics Prize]]. He was cited, "For his leadership role in the scientific endeavour that led to the discovery of the new Higgs-like particle by the [[ATLAS experiment|A Toroidal LHC ApparatuS]] (ATLAS) and [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] (CMS) collaborations at CERN's Large Hadron Collider".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/L53|title=Breakthrough Prize, Laureate Lyn Evans|website=breakthroughprize.org|access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>
*The [[Institute of Physics]] awarded him the [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize|Glazebrook Medal]] in 2013, citing him "for his leadership of the [[Large Hadron Collider]] Project".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/glazebrook/medallists/page_60379.html|title=2013 Glazebrook Medal|last=Physics|first=Institute of|website=iop.org|access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>
*He received the 2013 Special Breakthrough Prize, "For his leadership role in the scientific endeavour that led to the discovery of the new Higgs-like particle by the ATLAS and CMS collaborations at CERN's Large Hadron Collider".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L53|title=Breakthrough Prize|website=breakthroughprize.org|access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>
*He received the [[IEEE Simon Ramo Medal]] in 2014, for exceptional achievement in [[systems engineering]] and [[systems science]], "For systems leadership of the Large Hadron Collider Project from conceptual design through completion of construction".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieee.org/documents/ramo_rl.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100619214733/http://ieee.org/documents/ramo_rl.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 June 2010|title=IEEE Simon Ramo Medal Recipients|website=IEEE.org|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>
*He received the [[Rolf Wideroe Prize|Rolf Widerøe Prize]] in 2017<ref>{{Cite web|title=» Careers and people|url=http://live.iop-pp01.agh.sleek.net/2017/04/27/careers-and-people-29/|website=live.iop-pp01.agh.sleek.net|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref>
